title: Influence of Canopy on Acid‐Neutralizing Capacity of Base Cations in a Pine Plantation
content:
ABSTRACT

Forest canopy modification of atmospheric base cation deposition fundamentally influences ecosystem buffering against soil acidification. However, the effects of canopy-intercepted base cations on the acid-neutralizing capacity (ANC) delivered to the forest floor via throughfall (TF) remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the concentrations, fluxes and spatiotemporal patterns of TF base cations (K+, Ca2+, Mg2+ and Na+) at the event and intra-event scales in a Chinese pine (Pinus tabuliformis Carr.) plantation in Northern China. A neutralization factor was applied to quantify their relative contributions to the ANC of incident bulk precipitation (BP) and TF. Results showed that the enrichment in concentrations and fluxes of TF base cations was highest for K+, followed by Mg2+, Ca2+ and Na+. A canopy budget model revealed that canopy leaching dominated the net TF K+ and Mg2+ fluxes, whereas dry deposition primarily drove the Ca2+ flux. Spatially, TF base cation concentrations exhibited no significant correlations with either distance to the nearest trunk or canopy cover. Temporally, intra-event variations in TF base cations were qualitatively consistent with the antecedent dry period and rainfall intensity. Consequently, canopy-driven base cation enrichment significantly enhanced the event-level TF ANC compared to BP. Ca2+ remained the predominant neutralization factor for ANC in both BP and TF, followed by K+ and Mg2+. These findings demonstrate that the wash-off of dry-deposited Ca2+ and the canopy leaching of K+ and Mg2+ distinctly regulate the magnitude and direction of TF ANC, thereby acting as a critical buffer against incident rainfall acidity.
